item.title: How Does CPU Remember a Thread? Understanding Context Switch
item.description:
How Does CPU Remember a Thread? Understanding Context Switch

When we run multiple programs:


Browser

Database

Server

Compiler

It looks like they are running simultaneously.

But:

A single CPU core can execute only one instruction stream at a time.

So the question:

How can CPU switch between different threads and continue exactly where it stopped?

The answer:


Context Switch

item.title: How Does Linux Find the Real Socket From an Integer FD?
item.description:
How Does Linux Find the Real Socket From an Integer FD?

In the previous article, we learned:

int fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);

returns an integer.

But this creates another question:

If a socket is represented only by an integer, how does Linux find the real socket object inside the kernel?

For example:

read(fd, buffer, size);

The application only provides:

fd = 3

But inside the kernel, Linux needs to locate:

socket
TCP state
receive buffer
send buffer
protocol information
